name: nagare-architecture-refactor
globalChecks: cd web && npm run format:check && npm run test:ci

tasks.title: Extract persisted task-attempt transitions
tasks.objective: Create the authoritative module for persisted task-attempt claims, promotions, and completion transitions while preserving current external behavior.
tasks.architecture: Place a deep task-attempt transition module immediately above narrow transactional Store primitives. It owns transition validity, persisted compare-and-set behavior, and completion policy; it does not own caller side effects, transport, scheduling, or command execution.
acceptance: Claiming queued to running is a persisted compare-and-set: exactly one caller receives Applied, while a losing or replayed claim never authorizes dispatch.
Promoting pending to queued is conditional and cannot overwrite cancellation or another terminal state.
Completion centrally derives success, ordinary failure to up-for-retry or exhausted failure, terminal timeout failure, and cancellation replay from authoritative inputs.
An exact terminal replay returns AlreadyApplied, while a conflicting terminal outcome fails explicitly.
Invalid transitions leave status, output, timestamps, and attempt history unchanged.
The Store gains only the narrow atomic primitives required by the lifecycle module.
New deterministic module-boundary evals cover sequential claim replay and timeout with retries; baseline failure must not depend on scheduler timing or a stress-only race.
nonGoals: Do not split the entire Store abstraction.
Do not wire workers, the scheduler, or HTTP handlers in this task.
Do not own metrics, logs, transport, scheduling, or command execution.

tasks.title: Add atomic current-attempt control
tasks.objective: Deepen the lifecycle module with atomic logical-task cancellation and manual retry operations over the current attempt.
tasks.architecture: Extend the same task-attempt module rather than creating a second seam. Resolve current-attempt identity and perform cancellation or successor creation in database transactions so callers never reconstruct attempt history or coordinate correctness with process-local locks.
acceptance: Cancellation resolves and changes only the latest current attempt atomically for pending, queued, running, and up-for-retry states.
Repeated cancellation is idempotent and never rewrites historical attempts.
Manual retry validates the current attempt and inserts at most one successor atomically.
Cancellation racing retry cannot leave a queued or running successor after cancellation wins.
Manual retry preserves existing eligibility: current running or queued attempts are rejected, while pending, cancelled, up-for-retry, failed, and successful attempts remain retryable.
Database correctness does not rely on a process-local mutex.
New module-boundary evals deterministically exercise logical current-attempt cancellation, retry idempotency, and retry-versus-cancel serialization.
nonGoals: Do not wire worker, scheduler, or HTTP callers in this task.
Do not change public API payloads.
Do not broaden the lifecycle module into run-level progression.

tasks.title: Route local execution through task lifecycle
tasks.objective: Make the local worker a thin execution adapter over the task-attempt lifecycle while preserving its broker, executor, metrics, and process-cancellation responsibilities.
tasks.architecture: The worker may claim and complete attempts only through the lifecycle interface. Keep queue mechanics and external side effects local, ordered after authoritative persistence, and idempotently cleaned up.
acceptance: Dispatch claims through lifecycle before enqueue and delivers work only when the claim result is Applied.
Queue backpressure cannot strand an attempt in running: reserve capacity before claim or conditionally release an undispatched claim while preserving queued behavior.
An attempt cancelled after claim or enqueue but before running registration never executes.
Trigger-DAG, setup, empty-command, success, ordinary failure, timeout, and cancellation paths complete through lifecycle with local and remote retry parity.
A late local completion after cancellation preserves cancelled state and performs broker cleanup.
Broker cleanup is unconditional and idempotent; terminal metrics and logs occur only for a newly Applied lifecycle result.
Lifecycle persistence errors are propagated rather than discarded, with deterministic adapter evals for the claimed-then-cancelled execution window.
nonGoals: Do not change the lifecycle module or Store implementation.
Do not modify remote-worker transport.
Do not redesign executor interfaces beyond the smallest lifecycle adapter.

tasks.title: Route remote execution through task lifecycle
tasks.objective: Make Coordinator remote assignment and result handling a thin transport adapter over the task-attempt lifecycle.
tasks.architecture: Coordinator owns assignment identity, worker association, authoritative retry policy captured at claim, and idempotent transport-side cleanup. Persisted claim and completion validity remain inside the lifecycle module.
acceptance: Polling claims through lifecycle and returns work only when the claim result is Applied.
Coordinator records assignment ownership by attempt and worker and captures authoritative retry policy at claim; result handling never trusts worker-supplied retry counts.
Result ownership is validated and lifecycle persistence succeeds before live assignment state is discarded.
Ordinary remote failure matches local retry behavior and remote timeout remains terminal.
A replayed or late result releases worker accounting exactly once, cannot decrement a newer assignment, and still performs idempotent broker cleanup.
A late result after cancellation is accepted without overwriting cancellation; terminal metrics and logs occur only for an Applied result.
Deterministic adapter evals cover claimed retry policy and a replayed result while a newer assignment is active; concurrent polling may be a stress check but not the sole baseline-failure gate.
nonGoals: Do not change the lifecycle module or Store implementation.
Do not redesign the worker transport protocol.
Do not change public payloads unless an ownership identifier is demonstrably missing.

tasks.title: Wire lifecycle into scheduler and API orchestration
tasks.objective: Route scheduler and HTTP task-attempt orchestration through one production lifecycle service while preserving public behavior.
tasks.architecture: Production wiring shares the authoritative lifecycle service across Scheduler, local Pool, and Coordinator. Scheduler retains cadence and run-level concerns; HTTP remains a logical-task adapter and never reconstructs attempt identity.
acceptance: One lifecycle service is wired into Scheduler, local Pool, and Coordinator in production.
Pending promotion, setup failure, map-parent start and completion, delayed or manual retry, and run cancellation delegate attempt transitions to lifecycle.
Scheduler snapshots and broker side effects update only after authoritative persistence reports Applied; a lost transition race retains or reloads persisted state.
Killing a run cancels the latest current attempt in pending, queued, running, or up-for-retry state without rewriting attempt history.
The task-kill HTTP route uses run ID and logical task ID to cancel the current attempt, including a remote attempt.
Public request and response payloads and current manual-retry behavior remain unchanged.
Deterministic evals cover cancelling the latest retry attempt and resolving a logical task ID to its current attempt ID.
nonGoals: Do not add run-level progression policy in this task.
Do not redesign API payloads or scheduler cadence.
Do not change worker transport.

tasks.title: Extract authoritative run progression
tasks.objective: Create one authoritative service for promoting runnable tasks and deriving a run's terminal state after task-attempt changes.
tasks.architecture: Separate run-level dependency and terminal-state policy from scheduler ticking and persistence mechanics. Feed it task definitions and attempt snapshots; apply returned transitions through injected storage operations.
acceptance: A task becomes runnable exactly when every required predecessor has succeeded.
Failed, killed, and exhausted predecessor attempts prevent invalid downstream promotion.
Run terminal status is derived consistently after completion, retry exhaustion, and cancellation.
Repeated progression is idempotent and does not duplicate task instances.
Scheduler and retry paths use the same progression policy.
nonGoals: Do not replace cron scheduling.
Do not rewrite DAG parsing.
Do not introduce a general workflow engine abstraction.

tasks.title: Extract the run-inspection read model
tasks.objective: Create a cohesive read model for run details so the API and frontend consume consistent task, attempt, dependency, timing, and topology information.
tasks.architecture: Build the read model behind a narrow query interface. Keep storage queries and frontend rendering outside it; expose stable DTOs that can be projected into the shared execution topology.
acceptance: Run detail data distinguishes logical tasks from attempts without losing retry history.
Dependencies, timing, status, and logs metadata are assembled consistently in one query path.
The run page consumes the read model without reconstructing lifecycle semantics.
Existing run endpoints remain compatible or receive explicit compatibility adapters.
Read-model tests cover retries, mapped children, missing optional timing, and cancelled runs.
nonGoals: Do not build a general reporting subsystem.
Do not redesign unrelated dashboard pages.
Do not add a new database.
